meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Colombia (Unitary National Jurisdiction, no sub-state tax autonomy)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic tradition with a codified commercial code; Administrative and Constitutional law modeled on Continental European doctrine)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Colombia–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (Investment Chapter, in force 2012)
Colombia–Canada Free Trade Agreement (Investment Chapter, in force 2011)
Colombia–European Union Trade Agreement (Secondary rights of establishment and investment protections, in force 2013)
Colombia–United Kingdom Free Trade Agreement (continuity agreement, in force 2019)
Colombia–Spain BIT (1993) and Colombia–Spain Tax Treaty (2005)
Pacific Alliance Framework Agreement (Alianza del Pacífico)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 526 of 1999 (UIAF creation); Law 1121 of 2006 (AML/CFT preventive regime); Decree 1068 of 2015 (compilation of Decree 663 of 1993 prudential rules); Law 2155 of 2021 Article 170 (creation of the Registro de Beneficiarios Finales); DIAN Resolution 164 of 2021 (UBO identification and reporting parameters); DIAN Resolution 165 of 2023 (extension and filing mechanics); Superintendencia de Sociedades Circular Externa 100-000004 of 2021 (SISG-ALC self-regulation, risk-based due diligence); UIAF Circular 043 of 2020; Decreto 1736 of 2020 (tax administration beneficiary-owner definition)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Private Incorporation Deed of the S.A.S. (Documento Privado de Constitución) duly notarized and inscribed in the merchant register
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Authorized Notaría Pública in Colombia and the competent Cámara de Comercio
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Apostille Convention in force for Colombia since 4 October 2001; competent authority: Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores — Oficina de Legalizaciones)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal (Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation of the S.A.S.)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Cámara de Comercio (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores (Oficina de Legalizaciones)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing and Incumbency of the foreign corporate shareholder(s)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-State Companies Registry of the sole or majority shareholder (e.g., Delaware Division of Corporations; UK Companies House; Hong Kong Companies Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the home-state competent authority; if the home state has not acceded to the Hague Convention, Colombian Consular Legalization at the respective Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Spanish translation of foreign corporate documents (statutes, by-laws, powers of attorney, incumbency certificates)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Colombian-certified public translator (traductor oficial) or Ministry of Foreign Affairs-approved translation service
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization applied to the underlying source documents prior to or after translation, per recipient authority rules

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all incorporators, UBOs, representatives, and beneficial owners against OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, EU and UK restrictive measures lists, Interpol Red Notices (as available), UIAF and Colombian national penalties lists, and the Colombian Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) database maintained by the Financial Information and Analysis Unit (UIAF); enhanced customer due diligence and source-of-funds documentation required for PEPs and Medium-Risk Enhanced profiles under Circular Externa 100-000004 of 2021; mandatory reporting of suspicious transactions (ROS) to UIAF within prescribed statutory timelines; ongoing transaction monitoring with risk-rating recalibration minimum every six months.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) — official portal www.rues.org.co, operated jointly by the Chambers of Commerce of Colombia under the direction of the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC); filing is effected through the authorized Cámara de Comercio of the registered office address (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Article 107 of the Colombian Commercial Code requires the company name (denominación or razón social) to be expressed in Spanish; foreign expressions are admissible only when they constitute an existing denomination of a foreign parent or affiliate company or a trade-mark of recognized use, subject to the transliteration and homonymy rules issued by the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio; all documentary filings and the statutory name must be in Spanish, with accompanying apostilled translations for foreign-origin documents.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Sociedad Administradora de Fondos de Pensiones
Inversión (when used to imply a regulated collective investment scheme)
Arbitraje (when used to imply judicial or official functions)
Words in a language other than Spanish without documented use by the foreign parent
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of the proposed company name, the applicant may file a reconsideration petition (recurso de reposición) before the issuing Cámara de Comercio within 10 business days of notification, and a subsidiary appeal (recurso de apelación) before the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) within 10 business days following the chamber's final decision; the applicant may simultaneously submit one or more alternative name reservations to preserve the incorporation schedule; SIC resolves the appeal within statutory administrative deadlines and its decision is subject to judicial review before the Consejo de Estado in the event of continued denial.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible — for an ISIC 7310 digital media arbitrage and affiliate lead generation company, a virtual or administrative office may satisfy the registration address requirement only if a verifiable physical address within a Colombian municipality is designated for service of process, tax notifications, and Chamber of Commerce inspection purposes; the arrangement must not amount to a mere post-office box, and a physical location must be available for the sole corporate purpose and for any judicial or administrative summons; the branch-license regime for foreign entities is not triggered if the S.A.S. is a distinct Colombian legal person.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Nominal-to-moderate quantified risk of approximately 25% for unannounced physical on-site inspections within the first 24 months of operations; unannounced visits may be conducted by the Superintendencia de Sociedades under Decree 1074 of 2015, the DIAN, or municipal fiscal authorities when AML/CFT risk flags arise, when the registered address receives repeated returned notifications, or when the taxpayer's declared revenues materially diverge from its address profile; formal on-site inspections are rare in the advertising media-buying sector absent a triggering suspicious transaction report.

Merchant registry inscription fee (matrícula mercantil) of the company and registration of the deed

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores — Oficina de Legalizaciones

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Spanish translation and consular/apostille processing of foreign shareholder documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified public translator and courier agency
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per source document and page

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Sociedades por Acciones Simplificadas), especially Articles 1, 5, 12, 19, 22 and 27; supplemented by Código de Comercio, Decreto 410 de 1971, Articles 110-120.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; Mercantile Registry of Colombia, supervised by the Superintendencia de Sociedades.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento de Constitución (Private Instrument of Incorporation) submitted electronically through the RUES registry portal or filed in person at the Cámara de Comercio.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to an S.A.S. under Ley 1258/2008; capital may be expressed in any currency and paid in cash or in-kind, with the schedule of contributions specified in the bylaws. No escrow account is mandatory by law unless the shareholders voluntarily require it.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the accepted subscription and paid-in capital contributions be formally ratified as the fully subscribed share capital of Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada; that the principal registered office be established at the address set forth in the bylaws; that [Name] be appointed as legal representative (representante legal) and general manager, and [Name] as principal accounting officer; that the tax identification (NIT) registration and any required municipal operating permits be processed before the competent authorities; and that the legal representative be authorized to execute all documents required for incorporation, registration, and commencement of operations. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the secretary of the meeting certify this resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá (or local Cámara de Comercio chosen for the registered office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Request an availability certificate for the proposed corporate name by submitting the three preferred names to the Cámara de Comercio window or through the RUES electronic portal. The name is reserved for a non-extendable period of 30 calendar days pending submission of the incorporation document.
required_dossiers: Completed name availability form signed by the subscriber
Photocopy of the applicant's valid national ID or passport
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected due to similarity, immediately file the next preferred name from the alternate list; the system permits repeated searches and re-reservation without prejudice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Private Incorporation Document and Corporate Bylaws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The founder(s) directly or through an attorney; notarization is optional unless real property is contributed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the private instrument setting out the company's corporate purpose, capital subscription and payment schedule, share classes, board powers, representation clauses, and appointment of officers. Ensure the document bears civil and tax identification data of each subscriber and states the domicile, duration, and audit rights.
required_dossiers: Private deed (Documento de Constitución) satisfying Ley 1258/2008
Certified identification documents of subscribers
Acceptance letters of appointed legal representative and auditor if any
Capital contribution schedule and proof of monetary or in-kind valuation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or registry queries the document, amend the affected clauses by private simplification act and resubmit; any subscriber may execute an amendment, and the objection window is cured once the registry's observations are resolved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration in the Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio with jurisdiction over the company's registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed private incorporation document plus required annexes for registration. Pay the registration fee assessed on capital amount and complete the tax registration form (RUT). The registry confirms the incorporation and issues the 'Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal' upon approval.
required_dossiers: Executed private instrument of incorporation (Documento de Constitución)
Completed commercial registration application
FO-01, FO-02 and FO-03 forms of Cámara de Comercio
Payment receipt of registration and fees
Copies of NIT or upcoming NIT registration request if available
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration application is queried for missing annexes or formal defects, the company may cure by filing corrected documentation within 10 business days; the registry will freeze the registration date until complete information is submitted, after which the process resumes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Identification Number (NIT) Registration with DIAN
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company in the Unified Tax Registry (RUT) and obtain the NIT assignment. Filing may be completed electronically via the DIAN portal or at an authorized support center, using the commercial registration certificate and officer documentation. Attach the certificate of existence and legal representation if requested.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal issued by the Cámara de Comercio
Valid identification of the legal representative
Tax registration form (RUT)
Power of attorney if an agent performs the filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUT form is rejected due to inconsistencies between the commercial registry and DIAN records, correct the mismatched data with the Cámara de Comercio and then resubmit the RUT; DIAN applies a fresh five-business-day processing window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Workplace and Social Security Formality Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Caja de Compensación Familiar, ARL (Administradora de Riesgos Laborales), and EPS/PSY social security registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Notify staff and workplace information to the selected social security operator and ARL through the electronic system, and register any employee records accordingly. Also open a corporate bank account once the NIT and legal representation certificate are obtained, and activate the bank account signature card for the legal representative.
required_dossiers: Certificate of existence and legal representation
NIT tax identification document
Legal representative identification and company contact details
Corporate bank account application and beneficial owner declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If social security registration is objected, present the ARL form and employment contracts for confirmation; for banking issues, provide the current certificate of existence, updated within 90 days, and clarify the ultimate beneficial ownership chain.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial or manufacturing license is triggered by ISIC 7310 digital advertising and affiliate media buying activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no statutory operational license is mandatory for media buying services under Colombia's unified licensing framework.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) and local Corporaciones Autónomas Regionales (CARs)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-based digital media buying and affiliate lead generation involve no physical infrastructure or industrial discharge requiring a full EIA (Decree 1076/2015 exemption category).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC, or waste-handling thresholds apply to this activity; general municipal solid waste separation and water consumption rules may apply to the leased office premises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (Concepto Técnico de Bomberos) and structural occupancy clearance are required only for leased physical offices; a fully remote media-buying affiliate unit may comply with Ley 1221/2008 on telework and enroll employees in the ARL system for occupational health clearance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: DIAN – Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (Colombian Tax and Customs Authority). Official portal: https://www.dian.gov.co; transactional platform: MUISCA (https://muisca.dian.gov.co); foreign trade single window: VUCE (https://www.vuce.gov.co).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident establishing a Colombian S.A.S.: (1) Incorporate via Cámara de Comercio and obtain electronic registration certificate; (2) obtain a DIAN-accepted digital certificate (electronic signature class for MUISCA transactions); (3) register the company and its legal representative through MUISCA to obtain the NIT (9-digit tax ID) and RUT, expressly activating tax responsibilities 'renta – IVA – retención' and roles 'responsable de IVA' and 'facturador electrónico'; (4) for a foreign supplier of digital services without a Colombian establishment, use the simplified 'pre-RUT' registration process in MUISCA with a locally appointed apoderado; the NIT serves as the single TIN for income tax, VAT, customs and withholding at source.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or partnership-transparency election exists; an S.A.S. is opaque and taxed at the 35% corporate rate (2023 onwards), plus sectoral surcharges (financial entities 38%, oil/coal extractives up to 10% additional in certain windows). Electable mechanisms: (i) SIMPLE regime – optional combined income/VAT/municipal taxation for eligible small S.A.S. with prior-year gross revenue ≤3,500–6,800 UVT depending on activity (2025 UVT = COP 49,799); (ii) monthly VAT refund election for exporters of services ('devolución de saldos a favor' via MUISCA); (iii) tax consolidation within an economic group under Law 2277/2022 limits; (iv) hybrid mismatch self-correction disclosures under Article 130-1 ET (no proactive anti-hybrid election).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Impuesto a las Ventas – IVA; general invoice-credit value added tax regime under Articles 420 ff. Estatuto Tributario)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None for resident legal entities: an S.A.S. is a 'responsable de IVA' and must register for VAT/NIT regardless of turnover (Articles 437, 555-2 ET). Natural persons may remain in the simplified VAT regime if prior-year gross income < 3,500 UVT (≈ COP 174.3 million for 2025), but this exemption never extends to corporations. Non-resident digital platform/service suppliers (including affiliate ad exchanges contracting with Colombian end-users) must register as IVA collectors without any minimum threshold under Decree 1980/2020.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time fiscal clearance. Every IVA-responsible S.A.S. must issue 'Factura Electrónica de Venta' (FEV) through a DIAN-authorized technology provider (proveedor tecnológico) or DIAN's free SFE system, transmitting XML via web services/API to DIAN for instant cryptographic validation; each invoice must display the CUFE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica), DIAN acceptance status, and QR. Phased mandatory rollout is governed by Resolution DIAN 000165/2023 and subsequent calendars, covering substantially all taxpayers by the 2024–2025 cycles; export invoices, credit notes ('nota crédito'), debit notes and foreign-trade clearance documents must use the same validation channel through VUCE.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of services, including advertising and media-buying services (ISIC 7310), are IVA-excluded at 0% under Article 481(e) ET and DUT 1625/2016 Articles 1.3.1.7.1–1.3.1.7.4, provided: (i) the service is rendered in Colombia; (ii) the recipient is a non-resident entity with no domicile, branch or permanent establishment in Colombia; (iii) the service is effectively used or exploited exclusively outside Colombian territory; and (iv) the foreign currency consideration is channeled into the Colombian foreign-exchange market. Affiliate/performance media buying qualifies where the foreign client's end-advertiser, ad inventory, audience, or brand impact is located outside Colombia; campaigns aimed at Colombian consumers, Colombian website traffic, or local lead generation are in-country services subject to 19% IVA and cannot be zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: For services: VUCE Export of Services Declaration (Declaración de Exportación de Servicios) or equivalent service export certificate; commercial agreement / master service contract with the foreign counterparty; export invoice (factura de venta de exportación containing CUFE); bank evidence of receipt of foreign currency (inward SWIFT advice or certification by an authorized foreign-exchange intermediary); RUT page evidencing IVA responsibilities; work papers demonstrating exclusive foreign use or exploitation

For goods (if physical advertising inventory or printed materials are exported): customs export declaration (Declaración de Exportación, Form 110 through DIAN-WP system), Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill, and logistics certificates; single administrative document
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Ingreso de Divisas) confirming channeling of export proceeds through the Colombian exchange market
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN may deny the zero-rating retrospectively and assess the omitted 19% IVA plus default interest; falsified export documentation triggers the inexactness penalty of up to 160% of the tax evaded (Article 647 ET), e-invoicing and without-documentation penalties (Article 652-14 ET), possible establishment closures, and reopening of previous refund periods. Fraudulent zero-rating or false certificates are treated as tax evasion under Articles 402–403 of the Colombian Criminal Code as amended by Law 2277/2022, punishable by 4–9 years of imprisonment. Failure to channel foreign currency within 180 days is a foreign-exchange infraction under Decree 1368/2018 and Resolution 085/2020, subject to fines (up to 200% of the un-channeled amount), prohibition from exporter status, and loss of VAT refund eligibility.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (Central Bank of Colombia), operating with the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia as the local financial regulator and the foreign exchange intermediary channel in accordance with Decree 1735 of 1993 and Banco de la República's DCIN-83 regulations (Régimen de Cambios Internacionales).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia applies a single, free-floating exchange market with a reference rate (TRM) determined by market transactions. All foreign exchange operations must be transacted through authorized remittance intermediaries or banks. The Colombian peso is fully convertible for current-account purposes such as service import/export, dividends, interest, royalties, and profit repatriation, subject to compliance registration and foreign investment registration requirements. The capital account is open for non-resident equity investment and cross-border debt; the S.A.S. may receive equity injections without prior central bank authorization, but the foreign investment must be registered with the Banco de la República through the local bank to secure later dividend remittance rights. Profit remittance is allowed after the company is tax-domiciled, files annual corporate income tax returns, and provides audited financial statements proving distributable earnings; the S.A.S. must process the remittance through a bank's 'Declaración de Cambio' and the applicable withholding tax must be prepaid. No material convertibility restrictions apply to media-buying service receipts, but funds must enter Colombia through the formal FX market and cannot simply remain in offshore EMIs on a permanent basis without being disclosed as foreign assets.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Colombia does not impose a fixed percentage conversion of export receipts into COP, but imposes a mandatory 100% channeling and repatriation duty on service export proceeds. Receipts from digital advertising, performance media, and affiliate lead-generation services rendered to non-residents must be repatriated to Colombia and paid into an account held at an authorized foreign exchange intermediary (bank) using the applicable exchange declaration. The statutory timeline under DCIN-83 is that the exporter must initiate 'canalización' no later than the working day the foreign currency is available, and the Banco de la República grants a maximum retention period for service export proceeds; material export receipts must be declared and the underlying contract/invoice must be ready for audit. Any proceeds retained outside the formal market beyond the permitted term are considered non-channeled and are subject to coercive fines of up to USD 1,301 per infraction and potential suspicious-transaction reporting. In practice the bank will record 100% of the service export proceeds as received, convert to COP at the TRM to the extent needed for local expenses, and keep any unconverted balance in a permitted foreign-currency account at the same bank for approved outgoing FX payments.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational current account in COP with USD sub-account and treasury FX portal; share-capital escrow can be held temporarily on the same ledger
Operational current account in COP; USD account and international treasury desk for affiliate/media payables
Operational account and foreign-currency checking account; commercial letter-of-credit and trade-services desk

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BBVA Colombia (Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria Colombia S.A.)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Current account in COP, corporate internet banking with USD position and FX derivatives onboarding
COP/USD multi-currency account for digital businesses; enhanced EDD for online advertising
Corporate payment account with cross-border treasury services

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium as an ancillary collection/payment rail, Low as a substitute for Colombian FX channeling. Offshore EMIs such as Wise, Mercury, Airwallex, and Payoneer are not licensed Colombian foreign exchange intermediaries and cannot issue an account that complies with the S.A.S.'s FX channeling duty when receiving service-export revenue from overseas advertising platforms. The S.A.S. may use them for USD disbursements to publishers and vendors, but the funds that finance those disbursements must be traceable to a Colombian regulated account and the EMI balance must be reported as a foreign asset. Where inbound advertising revenue is collected by an EMI, the funds must be swept to a tier-1 Colombian bank in USD via SWIFT or converted into COP at a regulated bank to satisfy the channeling rule. If the S.A.S. wants to collect local card/ACH payments, it must contract with an SFC-authorized payment gateway or electronic funds institution; offshore EMIs cannot provide a COP account number or domicile the company's treasury in substitution for the local account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Most tier-1 Colombian banks require the legal representative to appear physically at least once, in person or through a Colombian notary/apostilled power of attorney, to authenticate the incorporation documents and sign the treasury mandate. Shareholders and non-signing directors may be interviewed by video conference or provide written KYC certificates. For an S.A.S. engaged in media buying, the bank's AML team will normally request a personal meeting with the UBO or its designated attorney-in-fact; a fully remote/electronically-signed account opening package is generally not accepted as the sole channel. The onboarding file must include certified copy of the 'Certificado de Cámara de Comercio', RUT, IDs of directors and UBOs, source-of-funds explanation, and an executed board resolution appointing the bank account signatories. Once the relationship is established, subsequent FX and treasury operations can be managed exclusively online/API.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk industry flag: affiliate marketing and pay-per-click media buying involve payments to a large number of unconnected publishers/ad networks, which can be interpreted as potential third-party payment layering or unlicensed money services business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A documented business model map showing traffic origin, ad-network payouts, S.A.S. revenue, and downstream publisher/vendor disbursements; master service agreements with each major platform; payment or payout reports from Google/Meta/TikTok/affiliate networks; ACH/SWIFT settlement logs; sub-affiliate onboarding and identity verification forms; monthly volume estimates; and an acceptable-use policy prohibiting sanctioned traffic.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of ultimate beneficial ownership: non-resident shareholders and multiple corporate layers conceal the natural persons ultimately controlling the S.A.S.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UBO declaration (as required by Colombian AML Law 2195 of 2022 and SFC Circular 029 of 2014) naming natural persons owning or controlling more than 10% where enhanced due diligence; corporate organization chart with percentages, passports of each UBO, proof of residential address, and a certified resolution confirming no bearer shares.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds mismatch on initial capital injection; the S.A.S. receives equity or shareholder loans but has little to no operating history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription agreement, bank statement evidencing transfer from known directors, Colombian tax filings (RUT, income tax returns), notarized source-of-wealth statement, and board minutes explaining the business model and forecast expenditure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and geolocation risk: programmatic traffic from, or payment flows to, OFAC/UN/Colombian-sanctioned jurisdictions or sanctioned Russian/Maduro-controlled actors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: IP/geo-targeting block certificates issued by the ad platform, terms and conditions of the media-plan platforms confirming prohibited territories, sanctions-list screening of all counterparties (or a third-party screening log), and a written sanctions/export-control compliance policy including jurisdiction blocks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of commercial substance: the S.A.S. appears to be a shell conduit routing funds from a U.S. parent to foreign publishers without Colombian operational substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease agreement for Colombian office, local payroll/pension contributions for employees, Colombian bank accounts, executed client service agreements showing the S.A.S. as principal, audited or reviewed financial statements, and a tax opinion confirming the S.A.S. has economic nexus in Colombia and is not a tax-transparent conduit.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injections from non-resident shareholders are routed via SWIFT MT103 from the parent/incorporator bank to the S.A.S.'s USD account at a Colombian tier-1 bank. The beneficiary must be exactly the S.A.S. NIT, and the payment reference must state the nature of the operation as 'Foreign direct investment – equity subscription' or 'share capital payment' rather than a commercial invoice. The Colombian receiving bank will request the foreign investment exchange declaration (Form 'Declaración de Cambio por Inversión Internacional') before crediting the funds, and the S.A.S. must register the foreign investment with the Banco de la República through the bank to obtain the registration certificate needed for future dividend repatriation. If the injection is a shareholder loan, use a separate cross-border debt registration (Form 'Declaración de Cambio por Endeudamiento Externo') and comply with transfer pricing requirements. All wires must show the true purpose code; the bank will reject 'consulting fees' or 'personal remittance' language for equity injections, because those codes trigger different withholding and tax treatment. When capital is injected entirely in COP, the initial FX conversion must still be done through the local bank's FX market and evidenced by the exchange declaration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound treasury payments for media-buying services are primarily service-import payments: the S.A.S. initiates a wire from its COP or USD account through the Colombian bank's international desk. The clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 (customer transfer) using the beneficiary bank's BIC, along with the signed counterparty contract and invoice. For large recurring payouts to ad networks/publishers, the bank maintains batch payment APIs or a treasury portal that screens all beneficiary names against sanctions lists and issues one aggregated FX declaration. Commercial letters of credit are generally unsuitable for pure digital advertising services; they are permissible only if the underlying agreement covers procurement of physical advertising media. For merchant payments, ACH/US local rails (via Wise or Mercury) can be used as long as the corresponding USD are classified as foreign funds already channeled to the Colombian bank and then disbursed locally; all outbound payments with an amount equal to or above USD 10,000, or any amount in foreign currency, must be submitted on the day of execution with an exchange declaration ('Declaración de Cambio' for services) through the local intermediary.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: COP/USD outright forward contracts entered into with SFC-regulated Colombian banks or brokerage firms, with an underlying media-buying trade forecast or balance-sheet exposure documented.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing the peso TRM, executed through an authorized local bank or an international dealer with reporting to Banco de la República; settlement in COP.
Cross-currency swaps between USD and COP for matched external debt, intercompany loans, or long-term supplier arrangements with an SFC-authorised lender.

Plain vanilla foreign-currency options to protect minimum media-spend commitments, provided the board approves the strategy and the contract is documented as a risk-management derivative with a registered dealer.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil (Annual Commercial Registry Renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 - March 31 annually; S.A.S. with December 31 year-end must renew, confirm legal representative, and report updated corporate data before April 1
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Surcharge of 10% of the renewal tariff per month or fraction of delay, capped at 100%; failure to renew for five consecutive years empowers the Chamber to dissolve/strike off the S.A.S. under Law 1258/2008

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Estados Financieros Anuales y Dictamen del Revisor Fiscal (Annual Financial Statements and Statutory Audit Opinion)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Asamblea de Accionistas (approval body); Cámara de Comercio; Superintendencia de Sociedades via SIRE when supervised
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be approved within three months of fiscal year-end (by March 31); supervised S.A.S. must submit year-end accounts through SIRE per the annual Supersociedades calendar, generally April - June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines under Law 222/1995 (up to SMLMV-based ceilings, potentially hundreds of thousands of USD for serious non-filing); SIRE late-filing penalties and loss of access to financing where accounts are not approved

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Información Anual de Beneficiario Final (Annual UBO Information Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales) under Resolución 000164 de 2021
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filing window set by DIAN for the preceding tax year; for fiscal year 2024, the return is due in the May - June 2025 calendar window, with the exact date published in the DIAN filing calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: DIAN penalty under E.T. Article 651: 1% of annual gross income, or 2,500 UVT (approx. USD 29,000) where no income, for non-filing; 0.5% for defective or late filing; UBO mismatches also expose the S.A.S. to anti-money-laundering review under the enhanced risk tier

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaración Anual de Inversión Extranjera / Formulario 4 (Annual Foreign Investment Update)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Banco de la República - Departamento de Cambios Internacionales (DCIN)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 following each fiscal year for non-resident shareholders holding registered foreign direct investment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Exchange-control penalties under Decree 1735/1993 for late or non-filing; de-registration of the foreign investment registration, blocking future dividend repatriation and capital remittance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Radicación y Actualización de Libros de Comercio (Statutory Books Registration and Share Register Updates)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio (book radicación) and corporate records kept at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Each new statutory book must be radicated with the Chamber before first use; share-transfer register entries and minutes of the annual shareholders' meeting must be current as of the March 31 renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unregistered books lose evidentiary weight in commercial litigation; Chamber fines apply for non-radicated books; failure to record transfers suspends the transferee's voting rights and creates UBO reporting mismatches

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A S.A.S. must appoint a Revisor Fiscal when, at December 31 of the prior year, any of the following is met: (a) gross assets equal or exceed 5,000 SMLMV (COP 7.12 billion, approx. USD 1.69 million); (b) gross income equals or exceeds 3,000 SMLMV (COP 4.27 billion, approx. USD 1.02 million); or (c) the company has more than 20 employees (Código de Comercio art. 203; Law 1258/2008 art. 28). Below these thresholds, statutory audit is optional unless required by bylaws.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Colombian GAAP as adopted IFRS: Grupo 1 (full NIIF/IFRS) for large companies; Grupo 2 (NIIF para PYMES / IFRS for SMEs) for most operating S.A.S.; Grupo 3 (NIIF para Microempresas) for micro entities with assets and revenue of 500 SMLMV or less and not more than 10 employees. Financial statements in COP, prepared under Decreto 2420/2015 as amended by Decreto 2270/2019, and filed in Spanish.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Colombia applies a look-through UBO rule: the S.A.S. must identify every natural person who directly or indirectly holds 5% or more of shares, exercises control under Law 1258/2008, or holds management/veto power, and must file the Beneficiario Final annual return with DIAN (Res. 000164/2021). Every share transfer must be recorded in the Register of Members before the transferee may exercise voting rights; at the annual shareholders' meeting (by March 31) the legal representative confirms the updated shareholding and UBO map, and any transfer to a non-resident entity requires a corresponding Banco de la República FDI register update. The Cámara de Comercio also collects Beneficiario Final data at the annual renewal.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Libro de Registro de Accionistas (Register of Members)
Libro de Actas de Asamblea (Minutes Book of the Shareholders' Meeting)
Libro de Registro de Junta Directiva (Register of Directors' Meetings), where a board exists
Libro Diario, Libro Mayor and Libro de Inventarios y Balances (statutory accounting ledgers)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - 900 per year for registered office and local agent services in Bogotá for a small S.A.S.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,200 - 3,500 for a SME S.A.S. Revisor Fiscal engagement, where the compulsory audit threshold is crossed

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 35% (Colombian corporate income tax rate for fiscal year 2024; Tax Code Article 49, Law 2277/2022 confirms 35%.)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday applies to ISIC 7310 affiliate media buying. The ordinary effective rate for this S.A.S. is 35% on Colombian-source net income after allowable deductions. Colombia grants limited exceptions (e.g., exemption for new creative/software companies under certain conditions, and sales rebates for audiovisual production under Law 1556/2012); an affiliate media-buying company does not qualify unless it is registered as a creative/software exporter and meets substance/employment thresholds. VAT at 19% may apply to separate invoicing; for income tax, standard deductions for media placement costs, platform fees, data/audience acquisition, and personnel costs are available.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 210 – Declaración de Renta y Complementario para Personas Jurídicas y Asimiladas, submitted electronically through the DIAN portal using the MUISCA/VUE system or certified electronic transmission service.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. The S.A.S. applies a fiscal year generally equal to the calendar year; the tax period is the twelve-month accounting period recognized by the DIAN.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate income tax return is due in the first quarter of the year following the tax period, on the specific date published by DIAN Resolution and determined by the last two digits of the taxpayer's NIT. For calendar-year S.A.S. filers, the deadline falls in April of the following year; any income tax balance payable must be settled by the same deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIT, registered legal name (razón social), and fiscal year identification. These fields must match the Cámara de Comercio registration and RUT data.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-owned S.A.S. files under its Colombian NIT. Do not substitute the foreign parent's tax identification; the S.A.S. is the Colombian taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All revenue attributable to the S.A.S., including affiliate commissions, media buying fees, performance-based advertising revenue, platform rebates, network incentives, and any ancillary income from digital advertising arbitrage.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross revenue received through Mercury, Wise, and wire-transfer rails; do not net out processing fees. Foreign-source income is included only if attributable to a Colombian PE or, for a Colombian resident entity, subject to worldwide taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Excluded income items, costs, expenses, and statutory deductions such as media placement costs, ad-server costs, traffic costs, affiliate payouts, salaries, social security contributions, and bank/gateway fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions for payments to foreign related parties are allowed only if the cost is necessary and proportional, subject to beneficial ownership, economic substance, and transfer-pricing documentation. Active non-resident owners must not directly deduct personal or parent-company expenses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of liquid ordinary net income after deductions, then comparison with presumptive income under Tax Code Article 188. The higher amount becomes the taxable base unless exemptions are substantiated.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Presumptive income applies to Colombian assets of the S.A.S.; non-resident shareholders' foreign assets are not considered. A loss-making S.A.S. must still assess renta presuntiva exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 63 / 64 (tax rate and principal income tax)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 35% statutory rate to the liquid taxable base, add alternative sanctions adjustments, and compute the final corporate income tax charge.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The S.A.S. determines tax at entity level; distributions to shareholders are taxed later at withholding level. If a Colombia PE of a foreign company is involved, use Form 110/115 for branch taxation; a S.A.S. is not a branch.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% of the tax due for each month or fraction of delay, capped at 100%, plus default interest. If no tax is due, penalties are computed under Tax Code Article 641 based on gross income/assets. Inaccurate returns: up to 200% of the omitted tax under Article 648. Criminal exposure for fraudulent omission exists under Law 1762/2015, with imprisonment of 3 to 9 years (extended for aggravated evasion).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% for non-resident shareholders on dividends paid out of profits already subject to the 35% corporate income tax (Tax Code Article 242). If dividends are paid from profits not taxed, or from tax-exempt income, additional shareholder-level tax of up to 35% applies on a look-through/grossed-up basis. No dividend withholding tax is imposed on the S.A.S. itself.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a Double Taxation Agreement (DTA), the non-resident shareholder must obtain a valid tax residence certificate (TRC/Certificado de Residencia Fiscal) from the tax authority of its jurisdiction, deliver it to the Colombian withholding agent before or on the payment date, and provide a beneficial ownership declaration. The S.A.S. should retain the TRC, board resolutions, distribution vouchers, and substance evidence for at least five years. No ex-ante DIAN approval is required; if the DTA rate is not applied, the non-resident may file a refund claim with the DIAN and append the TRC and supporting explanation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory source withholding rates: interest on debt and financial transactions: 15%; royalties and technical services: generally 20% under Tax Code Article 408, subject to treaty relief ranging from 0% to 15% depending on the DTA and the IP character of the payment. Software/affiliate technology payments that amount to transfer of an industrial or commercial intangible may be recharacterized and suffer higher royalty treatment. The S.A.S. must withhold and remit these amounts to DIAN within the statutory window; failure triggers a 100% penalty on the unwithheld amount plus default interest.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A mandatory Local File is required when the S.A.S.'s gross income or total assets at year-end exceed approximately COP 4,706,500,000 (100,000 UVT for tax year 2024, with UVT at COP 47,065). A Master File may also be required for qualifying multinational groups; taxpayers below the threshold must still file an informative return and support the arm's length nature of controlled transactions if engaged in related-party dealings above de minimis levels, especially with entities located in tax havens.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia has not enacted Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) for S.A.S. entities, but the DIAN and Colombian tax courts apply substance-over-form, Business Purpose Theory (Article 869-2 Tax Code), and OECD BEPS Action 5 substance principles in audits. An affiliate media-buying S.A.S. must demonstrate real commercial activity: executed media-buying contracts, active platform traffic management, local or contracted employees, commercial offices, managerial decisions, retained records, and operational bank accounts. A vehicle used solely as an invoicing/conduit for foreign advertising platforms may be disregarded and treated as a shell.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underreporting affiliate revenue or foreign rebates; inflating media placement costs with false invoices from shell suppliers; failing to file Form 210 after registering with the DIAN; concealing income received through Mercury/ACH/Wise into personal or foreign accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN inexactitude penalty up to 200% of the understated tax; late-filing and omission penalties of 5% per month; default interest; criminal tax evasion under Law 1762/2015 carries imprisonment from 3 to 9 years and closure/cancellation of the RUT in grave cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Veil-piercing under Commercial Code Article 71 can impose joint civil liability; directors and legal representatives may be required to personally restitute the evaded tax, are exposed to asset embargoes and travel bans, and may be criminally prosecuted as co-authors of fraudulent returns.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a nominal S.A.S. without office, personnel, bank account activity, board minutes, or actual managerial control; routing affiliate revenue through the entity only to generate deductible costs for a foreign principal; failing to demonstrate business purpose in DTA benefit claims.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DIAN may disregard the S.A.S., attribute the income to the real foreign beneficiary, impose a 200% inaccurate-return penalty, levy default interest, and administratively deactivate the tax identification (RUT). Commercial cancellation and professional disqualification may also be ordered.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Administrators, shareholders, and beneficial owners who deliberately maintain a shell S.A.S. are jointly liable for taxes, penalties, and third-party damages; criminal liability can include money laundering where funds from staged transactions are repatriated, with preventive detention and exit bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Documentary Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling affiliate media-buying services to a foreign related party at a margin below arm's length; paying excessive management fees to an offshore affiliate; failing to prepare Local/Master File documentation above the statutory threshold; providing a defective comparability analysis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DIAN recharacterizes the transaction at the arm's length price and assesses the resulting tax difference, plus a penitential adjustment of up to 200% of the tax understatement or 100% of the TP adjustment, default interest, and separate penalties for non-filing of the TP informative return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and CFOs who approve false intercompany pricing tables may be jointly liable for the corporate tax deficiencies; accounting professionals involved in preparing false TP studies are exposed to administrative disqualification and civil restitution; criminal liability attaches if fraudulent invoices or documents are used.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Characterizing actual dividend distributions as tax-deductible interest, fictitious royalties, or technical service payments to avoid the 5% dividend withholding tax; issuing shareholder loans with no repayment schedule or economic substance; using intercompany accounts to strip profits out of Colombia without DTA compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of the payment as a dividend triggers the 5% or additional shareholder-level dividend tax, gross-up, default interest, and a penalty of up to 200% of the underwithheld amount. The foreign recipient remains liable for Colombian-source tax; a DTA does not protect disguised equity distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives who sign loan agreements or service contracts without business purpose are personally liable for unpaid withholding; criminal charges may include fraudulent breach of duty and conspiracy to evade taxes, with travel bans and seizure of personal assets during investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving affiliate advertising commissions from counterparties under investigation for ad fraud, undisclosed shell platforms, or sanctioned networks via Mercury, Wise, or wire transfers without sufficient KYB/KYC and source-of-funds records; funneling funds to conceal true ultimate beneficial owners; using accounts to mix business income with suspicious proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Colombia criminalizes money laundering under Law 599/2000 (Articles 323-327) with imprisonment from 10 to 30 years and fines of up to hundreds of thousands of statutory minimum monthly wages. The S.A.S. may be subject to asset forfeiture under Law 1708/2014, cancellation of commercial registration, and blacklisting by the UIAF.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Veil-piercing is permitted where corporate form is used to launder illicit proceeds; directors and beneficial owners face extradition, travel bans, personal asset confiscation, severe civil restitution claims by victims, and loss of legal right to administer Colombian companies.
